The caterpillar reaches 10 pounds after **9217 days**.

**Setup.** At weight $w$ he moves at speed $2^{-w}$, so covering distance $d$ takes $d \cdot 2^{w}$ days. Eaten fruits no longer stop him, so each leg runs from the last fruit eaten on one side to the nearest uneaten fruit on the other side.

**Legs.** Each leg from weight $w$ to $w+1$ has length $w+1$:

| Weight $w \to w+1$ | Route | Distance | Speed | Days |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 → 1 | 0 → 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| 1 → 2 | 1 → −1 | 2 | 1/2 | 4 |
| 2 → 3 | −1 → 2 | 3 | 1/4 | 12 |
| 3 → 4 | 2 → −2 | 4 | 1/8 | 32 |
| 4 → 5 | −2 → 3 | 5 | 1/16 | 80 |
| 5 → 6 | 3 → −3 | 6 | 1/32 | 192 |
| 6 → 7 | −3 → 4 | 7 | 1/64 | 448 |
| 7 → 8 | 4 → −4 | 8 | 1/128 | 1024 |
| 8 → 9 | −4 → 5 | 9 | 1/256 | 2304 |
| 9 → 10 | 5 → −5 | 10 | 1/512 | 5120 |

**Total.** The time is $\sum_{w=0}^{9} (w+1)\,2^{w}$. Using $\sum_{k=1}^{n} k\,2^{k-1} = (n-1)2^n + 1$ with $n=10$ gives $9\cdot 1024 + 1 = 9217$. The table sums to the same value.

ANSWER: 9217
